findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py (a new schema-name constant + OUTPUT_SCHEMAS synthetic-key entry) and, per the overlap_verdict idiom, the corresponding src/rebar/schemas/<epic_bug_screen_verdict>.schema.json to Scope, since the every-schema-file-is-wired CI guard requires both beyond contracts.py.
evidence: The reference idiom overlap_verdict is registered in THREE places, not one: src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:236 `register_contract("overlap_verdict", ...)`; src/rebar/schemas/overlap_verdict.schema.json (a standalone JSON schema file); and src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:130 `OVERLAP_VERDICT = "overlap_verdict"` plus the OUTPUT_SCHEMAS entry at :318 under the synthetic key `"overlap_judge": OVERLAP_VERDICT`.

src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py comments repeatedly cite an 'every-schema-file-is-wired guard' (:120, :124, :139, :306, :313, :321, :326, :341) that fails CI when a schema file or registration is missing.

The overlap_judge.md prompt front-matter uses `outputs: overlap_verdict` (:7) — the exact shape the plan mirrors with `outputs: epic_bug_screen_verdict` — confirming the prompt->schema->schemas/__init__ wiring chain the new schema must replicate.

The plan's Scope line names only contracts.py for the new schema; src/rebar/schemas/overlap_verdict.schema.json's analog (epic_bug_screen_verdict.schema.json) and the src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py constant+OUTPUT_SCHEMAS entry are absent from Scope.
findings.finding: The plan adopts the overlap_verdict schema idiom for the new epic_bug_screen_verdict schema but scopes the schema registration to src/rebar/llm/contracts.py only; the overlap_verdict idiom is actually wired across three files, so two edit targets are unenumerated and a CI guard will fail.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/epic_bug_screen.md (new prompt, `outputs: epic_bug_screen_verdict`) + src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (schema + normalizing validator, overlap_verdict idiom)'
scenarios: Implementer registers epic_bug_screen_verdict in contracts.py only, per Scope; the every-schema-file-is-wired drift gate fails CI because no schemas/__init__.py entry (and possibly no .schema.json file) exists for it.
The runner/validator cannot resolve the new output schema at gate runtime because the schemas package registry lacks the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Scope schema line to: 'src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (register_contract + normalizing validator) + src/rebar/schemas/epic_bug_screen_verdict.schema.json + src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py (EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_VERDICT constant + OUTPUT_SCHEMAS synthetic-key entry) so the every-schema-file-is-wired drift gate passes' — mirroring how overlap_verdict is wired at contracts.py:236, schemas/overlap_verdict.schema.json, and schemas/__init__.py:130/:318.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the 32-candidate screen ceiling and the 8-candidate forwarding cap are module constants or config-surfaced, so the operator-visible overflow tally has an actionable tuning path.
evidence: 'at most 32 candidates are evaluated per close ... any remainder is recorded in the sidecar tally as an unevaluated-overflow count (visible to the operator)'
findings.finding: The screen ceiling (32 candidates) and the forwarding cap (8) are hardcoded magic numbers derived from the backtest, but the plan surfaces an unevaluated-overflow tally to the operator — implying these are operational tuning knobs likely to evolve — without stating whether they are configurable or where they live.
findings.location: Approach stage 2 ('Enforced screen ceiling: at most 32 candidates') and forwarding ('cap 8')
scenarios: Operator observes recurring overflow and wants to raise the ceiling without a code edit
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the ceiling/cap are named module-level constants (or config keys) so they can be adjusted from the overflow tally without touching gate logic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Weigh the screen's per-candidate fan-out against the codebase's existing batched judge idiom (llm/overlap/judge.py::judge_batch + overlap_verdict_batch): either adopt a batched call (shared epic material hoisted into the cached system prompt, one entry per candidate, per-candidate abstain + label-not-position matching) or state the positive reason per-candidate isolation is required here.
evidence: Plan: 'Haiku relevance screen: single-turn per candidate ... one warm call then parallel fan-out, reusing the warm-then-fan-out orchestration pattern of plan_review/pass1.py'

src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py:148 judge_batch — 'ONE judge call carrying shared against every candidate in pairs, returning {candidate_id: verdict}'; _CANDIDATES_PER_CALL=6 bounded to contain cross-contamination; per-candidate abstain on missing/malformed; label-not-position matching

src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:201-225 overlap_verdict_batch — a LIST of verdicts, one entry per candidate, subclassing the single-pair model (the same schema idiom the plan cites at contracts.py:175 for its epic_bug_screen_verdict)
pass1 (pass1.py:196-201) warms then fans per-CHUNK where each call has distinct material; it is NOT the 'one shared thing vs. N candidates' shape the screen actually has
findings.finding: The screen's orchestration is specified as PER-CANDIDATE fan-out (one call per candidate, up to the 32-candidate ceiling) citing plan_review/pass1's warm-then-fan-out, but pass1 fans per-CHUNK with DISTINCT material per call. The screen's actual shape — ONE shared epic judged against N candidate bugs, precision-sensitive, one-line citation each, degrade-open — is the exact shape the codebase already implements as a BATCHED call in llm/overlap/judge.py::judge_batch (overlap_verdict_batch schema, shared digest hoisted into the cached system prompt, label-not-position matching, per-candidate abstain, whole-batch degrade), using the very same overlap_verdict schema family the plan mirrors for its output contract. The plan does not weigh this batched alternative, which would cut up-to-32 calls per close to a handful while inheriting the per-candidate-degrade robustness the screen needs.
findings.location: Approach, stage 3 ('single-turn per candidate ... one warm call then parallel fan-out, reusing the warm-then-fan-out orchestration pattern of plan_review/pass1.py')
scenarios: An epic close with a large candidate set (backtest p90=11, max=24; ceiling 32): per-candidate fan-out issues up to ~24-32 haiku calls where judge_batch would issue ~4-6, multiplying latency and per-close cost with no accuracy gain

Small epics below the 4096-token cache floor (bug 7a79): per-candidate fan-out pays the epic-material prompt on EVERY uncached call; a batched call amortizes the shared epic material across all candidates in a single request
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the judge_batch shape for the screen: hoist the epic material (title/description/AC/children titles) into the cached system prompt once, list the candidate bugs in one user message keyed by ticket id, and bind the existing overlap_verdict_batch-style schema (a list of {ticket_id, verdict A/B/C, citation}) with the same per-candidate abstain-to-C degrade and label-not-position matching. Bound batch size (as _CANDIDATES_PER_CALL=6 does) to contain cross-candidate contamination; if the total exceeds the batch bound, issue a few batched calls rather than up to 32 single-candidate calls. Keep the 32-candidate screen ceiling and overflow tally unchanged. If per-candidate isolation is genuinely required (e.g. citation quality measured to degrade in batches), state that as the positive rationale instead.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge overlap/judge.py (epic only-crave-art) as the closest in-repo prior art for the stage-3 screen and either reuse its classifier scaffolding or state why a lighter single-turn per-candidate screen is the right divergence (e.g. haiku cost, C-default degrade-open, DET floor as the hard tier), explicitly addressing the dropped dual-ordering/agreement gate.
evidence: Plan: 'Haiku relevance screen: single-turn per candidate, forced choice {A/B/C} + one-line citation'
Plan cites the schema idiom only: 'Screen output contract follows the overlap_verdict idiom (contracts.py:175)' — no mention of overlap/judge.py as the classifier design precedent

judge.py:1-9 docstring: bounded LLM pairwise classifier over K candidates, judged in BOTH orderings, surfaced only when both orderings agree + cite a concrete artifact + clear a confidence threshold; 'Surfaces at most overlap_surface_cap advisory findings; NEVER auto-links'
judge.py:62-66: _CANDIDATES_PER_CALL=6 is bounded 'rather than all of them' to contain 'the cross-contamination risk the prompt's per-candidate independence rules exist to contain'
judge.py:112-125: overlap-judge already binds the model-class table per call and documents bug afeb — the same constraint the plan cites for its screen
findings.finding: The stage-3 haiku relevance screen is a bounded per-candidate LLM classifier at a ticket-relation gate — the same architectural family as the repo's existing overlap-judge (src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py, epic only-crave-art) — but the plan treats the classifier design as green-field. It reuses only that system's overlap_verdict SCHEMA idiom (contracts.py:175) and does not acknowledge the judge itself as prior art, nor justify diverging from two deliberate precision-hardening choices the judge made: dual-ordering position-bias mitigation with a both-orderings-agree gate, and a bounded candidates-per-call batch (_CANDIDATES_PER_CALL=6) chosen specifically to contain cross-candidate contamination.
findings.location: Approach stage 3 (Haiku relevance screen); Scope: src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py
scenarios: The single-turn-per-candidate screen inherits position/framing bias the overlap-judge deliberately mitigates, and a reviewer later asks why the two ticket-relation LLM gates diverge in rigor with no recorded rationale.
A future maintainer duplicates classifier plumbing (prompt-caching, per-candidate structured output, abstain/safe-default handling) that overlap/judge.py already solves.
findings.suggested_fix: In the stage-3 paragraph, add a sentence noting the overlap-judge as the design precedent and justify the divergence: the screen tolerates single-turn (no dual-ordering) because a garbled/biased verdict defaults to C (non-surfacing), the DET floor is the hard tier, and any A-verdict is only advisory input to the verifier's store-grounded adjudication — so screen false-negatives degrade open rather than fabricating a block. If any classifier scaffolding (structured single_turn call + safe-default validator + cache-warm fan-out) lifts cleanly from the overlap path, reuse it; otherwise mirror with a citation comment (no speculative refactor).

findings.finding: The verifier's disposition adjudication (block only an undispositioned deliverable-defect; SATISFY via supersedes/duplicates link or reasoned pre-existence prose) is the core novel behavior that separates the must-block fixtures (30a2, 5b09) from the must-pass fixtures (30d3 prose, e6a0 link, c8ed link) — but the plan states automated tests 'drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map' and the sole live acceptance criterion covers only the screen's A/B/C -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path, not the live verifier's disposition decision over those fixtures. If both the screen verdict and the verifier verdict are faked, the must-block/must-pass regression assertions validate only plumbing while the disposition rule — the riskiest new logic — never runs as it will in production.
findings.location: Testing section ('All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs') and AC line 9 ([operator-attested] live calibration run 'proving the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path')
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion that the live calibration run also records the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture (proving 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass and 30a2/5b09 block through the real disposition rule), keeping the automated suite on the fake map for the screen only.

findings.finding: The plan states all automated regression tests drive the SCREEN through a fake forced-choice verdict map, but leaves unspecified whether the VERIFIER's adjudication (the actual block/pass decision the must-block/must-pass fixtures assert) is faked or live in those automated tests. The verifier is itself an LLM (completion_verifier.md); if it is not faked, the automated must-block/must-pass tests are non-deterministic and cannot be a proving command; if it IS faked, then AC5's disposition rule (store-grounded a/b signals) is only actually exercised by the operator-attested live run, and the automated tests prove only DET floor + forwarding plumbing.
findings.location: Testing section ('drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map') vs AC line 5 ('verified by the must-block/must-pass regression fixtures') and AC line 8
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add: 'Automated tests fake BOTH the screen verdict map AND stub the verifier decision path (or assert only up to the forwarded candidate block); the verifier's real store-grounded block/pass per fixture is validated exclusively by the AC10 operator-attested calibration run, so no CI test depends on live LLM judgment.'

findings.finding: The DET caused_by floor's ENFORCEMENT (the deterministic short-circuit BLOCK that skips the LLM, analogous to the direct-children gate) must be wired into the completion_precheck op in gate_ops.py — the same place the unclosed-child short-circuit lives (gate_ops.py:63-74, returning run_verify=False + a FAIL verdict so the ELSE/passthrough arm is taken) — but the plan's Scope entry for gate_ops.py names ONLY 'append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change', and the completion.py entry names only the floor detection + candidate filter. The floor's block-wiring in completion_precheck is left unenumerated.
findings.location: Scope: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py and src/rebar/llm/completion.py entries; Approach stage 1
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the gate_ops.py Scope bullet to read '(completion_precheck: DET-floor short-circuit BLOCK mirroring the unclosed-child gate — run_verify=False + deterministic FAIL verdict; AND append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change)', and note in the completion.py bullet that it supplies the floor DETECTION helper consumed by that short-circuit.
